learning_outcomes.text: The purpose of this module is to provide the student with complementary knowledge of electrotechnics.
The objective of this course is to provide the basis of quasi-static electromagnetic fields, DC and AC electrical circuits, electrical machines, power supply systems and electrical safety.
After the completion of this module, the student should understand the fundamental concepts of electrical systems and their applications.
The student must be able to solve electrical circuits and simple field configurations.
The student must also know the basic notions of electrical energy and electrification.

syllabus_topics: EXERCISES (solving exercises on electrical circuits done at home and in class.)
SEMINARS (in-depth studies on innovative electrotechnical topics for industrial engineering).
INTRODUCTION TO THE COURSE. Introduction to electrotechnics and the course.

THE ELECTRIC FIELD. Fundamental concepts and definitions. Fundamental laws. Displacement current. Image method. Dielectric properties of materials. Electric field produced by simple charge distributions. Capacitance. Capacitor connections. Planar and cylindrical capacitors. Partial capacitances.
THE CURRENT FIELD. Fundamental concepts and definitions. Fundamental laws. Material conductivity. Resistance. Resistor connections. Kirchhoff's methods. Current dispersers. Earth resistance.

THE MAGNETIC FIELD. Fundamental concepts and definitions. Fundamental laws. Magnetic field produced by simple current distributions. Magnetic properties of materials. Electromagnetic induction phenomena. Magnetic circuits. Self and mutual inductance.

DC CIRCUITS AND NETWORKS. Fundamental electrical quantities. Ohm's Law. Joule's Law. Resistance and conductance. Series and parallel connections, star and delta. Delta-star transformation. Ideal and real voltage and current generator. Kirchhoff's Principles. Thevenin's Theorem. Tellegen's Theorem. Superposition Principle. Graph, tree, and co-tree of a network. Node method. Mesh method.

CIRCUITS IN PERMANENT SINUSOIDAL REGIME. Sinusoidal periodic quantities: definitions and terminology. Representations of isofrequency sinusoidal functions using phasors and complex numbers. Elementary operations on phasor quantities. Instantaneous, active, reactive, and apparent power in permanent sinusoidal regime. Study of circuits in permanent sinusoidal regime. Node and mesh method. Voltage drop. Power factor correction. Series resonance.

THREE-PHASE SYSTEMS. Symmetric and balanced three-phase systems. Star and delta connection. Instantaneous, active, reactive, and apparent power in symmetric and balanced three-phase systems. Analysis of three-phase circuits.
INTRODUCTION TO ELECTRICAL MACHINES. Generalities and construction notes. Induced e.m.f. Rotating magnetic field. Notes on traditional electrical machines and converters.

TRANSFORMERS. Generalities and construction notes. Theory of the single-phase transformer. Ideal transformer. No-load, on-load, and short-circuit operation. Equivalent electrical circuit of the single-phase transformer. Energy balance and efficiency. Nameplate data. Notes on three-phase transformers.

ASYNCHRONOUS MACHINES. Generalities and construction notes. Theory of operation with stationary and moving rotor. Mathematical model and equivalent electrical network. Energy balance. Mechanical characteristic. Starting of asynchronous motors.
ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS. Main uses of electrical energy. Generation, transmission, distribution, and use of electrical energy. Electrical safety.
assessment_rules: The oral exam aims to ascertain theoretical preparation, logical rigor, and the ability to solve problems by applying acquired knowledge. The grade attribution will reflect the following preparation levels: sufficient (18-22) for basic understanding, good (23-26) for full understanding, and excellent (27-30) for the ability to apply learned theory and solve problems.
